The method sets emission and absorption volumes to the same data source, sets the reflection volume to a constant value of 1 for each voxel, and applies scaling factors globally or per-voxel [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in Section 3.3.2 that 'The emission and absorption volumes were set to the same data' and 'The reflection volume was set to 1 for each voxel.' Furthermore, Section 4.2 confirms that scaling factors (k_em, k_ab, k_ref) can be applied 'for an entire volume by a scalar' (globally) or 'at a fine granular scale for each voxel by defining distinct volumes' (per-voxel).

A rendering approach using separate volumes for emission, absorption, and reflection to simulate material light properties, with gradients computed on the fly by the GPU [S1].

The claim states that the rendering approach uses separate volumes for emission, absorption, and reflection to simulate material light properties, with gradients computed on the fly by the GPU. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 4.2 ('Volume Design'), stating: 'Our renderer supports the capability to define each volume, i.e., emission, absorption, and reflection, allowing for custom renderings to simulate different materials with different light properties.' Additionally, Section 3.3.2 ('Scene') confirms: 'The gradient was computed on the fly by the GPU.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
